question: When driving uphill in second gear, what gear should be used going downhill?
options: (1) Fourth gear.
(2) Third gear.
(3) Second gear.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (3) is Correct: When driving downhill, you must NEVER turn off the engine or coast in neutral (N). Turning off the engine cuts off the vacuum brake booster and hydraulic power steering, resulting in near-total loss of braking ability and steering control. In addition, shifting to a lower gear utilizes 'Engine Braking', preventing brake pads from overheating and suffering catastrophic brake fade.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (Fourth gear.): Coasting in neutral or turning off the engine removes all engine braking, leading to overheated boiled brake fluid and brake failure.
• Option (2) (Third gear.): Riding the foot brake continuously causes extreme friction heat and sudden brake loss.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!

question: Regarding the use of engine braking to assist in controlling speed on long downhill sections, which of the following statements is correct?

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:

• Option (3) (Regardless of manual or automatic transmission, engine braking is sufficient to handle all downhill situations and no additional use of the foot brake is necessary.): Riding the foot brake continuously causes extreme friction heat and sudden brake loss.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!

question: For an automatic transmission vehicle, in which gear position is it NOT permitted to start the engine?
options: (1) N (Neutral).
(2) P (Park).
(3) R (Reverse).
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (3) is Correct: Automatic vehicles are equipped with a starter safety inhibitor switch. The engine will only crank when the gear selector is in 'P' (Park) or 'N' (Neutral), and the driver must firmly press the foot brake to prevent the vehicle from lurching forward or backward upon ignition.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (N (Neutral).): Starting in D (Drive) or R (Reverse) is prevented by safety interlocks to avoid sudden unintended acceleration into pedestrians or walls.
• Option (2) (P (Park).): Starting without pressing the brake allows the car to roll away uncontrollably on gradients.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Automatic Start: Shift to P (Park) + Press Foot Brake before turning ignition key/pushing start!

question: When a vehicle is traveling on a freeway under normal weather conditions at a speed of 100 kilometers per hour, what is the minimum safe following distance between vehicles?
options: (1) 80 meters for large vehicles, 50 meters for small vehicles.
(2) 90 meters for large vehicles, 50 meters for small vehicles.
(3) 80 meters for large vehicles, 60 meters for small vehicles.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (1) is Correct: Taiwan Freeway Safety Distance Formula:
• Small Passenger Cars: Speed ÷ 2 in meters ➔ 100 km/h ÷ 2 = 50 meters.
• Large Vehicles (Trucks/Buses): Speed - 20 in meters ➔ 100 km/h - 20 = 80 meters.
Large vehicles have much greater mass and momentum, requiring significantly longer distance to bring to a complete stop.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (2) (90 meters for large vehicles, 50 meters for small vehicles.): Incorrect distance calculation that does not provide sufficient emergency reaction and braking buffer.
• Option (3) (80 meters for large vehicles, 60 meters for small vehicles.): Violates official Highway Bureau safe following distance standards.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Freeway Rule: Small Cars = Speed / 2; Large Trucks = Speed - 20 (double in rain/fog)!

question: When a vehicle reaches an uphill and downhill slope of approximately equal gradient, if 2nd gear is used going uphill, which gear should be selected going downhill to achieve fuel efficiency, safety, and time savings?
options: (1) Drive in 3rd or 4th gear.
(2) Shift into neutral (N gear).
(3) Drive in 2nd or 1st gear.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (3) is Correct: When driving downhill, you must NEVER turn off the engine or coast in neutral (N). Turning off the engine cuts off the vacuum brake booster and hydraulic power steering, resulting in near-total loss of braking ability and steering control. In addition, shifting to a lower gear utilizes 'Engine Braking', preventing brake pads from overheating and suffering catastrophic brake fade.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (Drive in 3rd or 4th gear.): Coasting in neutral or turning off the engine removes all engine braking, leading to overheated boiled brake fluid and brake failure.
• Option (2) (Shift into neutral (N gear).): Riding the foot brake continuously causes extreme friction heat and sudden brake loss.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!

question: A large truck is traveling in the slow lane on a downhill slope in rainy weather with poor visibility. 💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!

question: When driving on a freeway and encountering dense fog, heavy smoke, strong winds, heavy rain, nighttime driving, or other special conditions, what safe following distance should be maintained from the vehicle ahead?

Large vehicles have much greater mass and momentum, requiring significantly longer distance to bring to a complete stop.

• Option (2) (Small vehicles adopt the safe following distance of large vehicles; the safe following distance for large vehicles remains unchanged.): Violates official Highway Bureau safe following distance standards.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Freeway Rule: Small Cars = Speed / 2; Large Trucks = Speed - 20 (double in rain/fog)!

question: Under normal weather conditions, when a small car is traveling on a freeway or expressway at 90 km/h, what is the minimum safe following distance that should be maintained between two consecutive vehicles?

• Small Passenger Cars: Speed ÷ 2 in meters ➔ 90 km/h ÷ 2 = 45 meters.
• Large Vehicles (Trucks/Buses): Speed - 20 in meters ➔ 90 km/h - 20 = 70 meters.
Large vehicles have much greater mass and momentum, requiring significantly longer distance to bring to a complete stop.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (30 meters or more.): Incorrect distance calculation that does not provide sufficient emergency reaction and braking buffer.
• Option (3) (60 meters or more.): Violates official Highway Bureau safe following distance standards.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Freeway Rule: Small Cars = Speed / 2; Large Trucks = Speed - 20 (double in rain/fog)!

question: When a vehicle is traveling on a freeway, expressway, or a road with controlled access points, and fails to maintain the required safe following distance, which of the following penalties is correct?

explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (2) is Correct: Taiwan Freeway Safety Distance Formula:
• Small Passenger Cars: Speed ÷ 2 in meters ➔ 90 km/h ÷ 2 = 45 meters.
• Large Vehicles (Trucks/Buses): Speed - 20 in meters ➔ 90 km/h - 20 = 70 meters.
Large vehicles have much greater mass and momentum, requiring significantly longer distance to bring to a complete stop.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (A fine of NT$1,200–2,400 and suspension of the driver's license for 1 month.): Incorrect distance calculation that does not provide sufficient emergency reaction and braking buffer.
• Option (3) (A fine of NT$6,000–12,000 and immediate revocation of the driver's license on the spot.): Violates official Highway Bureau safe following distance standards.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Freeway Rule: Small Cars = Speed / 2; Large Trucks = Speed - 20 (double in rain/fog)!

question: When driving downhill:
options: (1) Turn off the engine and coast in neutral to save fuel.
(2) For safety, never turn off the engine and coast in neutral.
(3) No gear change needed.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (2) is Correct: When driving downhill, you must NEVER turn off the engine or coast in neutral (N). Turning off the engine cuts off the vacuum brake booster and hydraulic power steering, resulting in near-total loss of braking ability and steering control. In addition, shifting to a lower gear utilizes 'Engine Braking', preventing brake pads from overheating and suffering catastrophic brake fade.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (Turn off the engine and coast in neutral to save fuel.): Coasting in neutral or turning off the engine removes all engine braking, leading to overheated boiled brake fluid and brake failure.
• Option (3) (No gear change needed.): Riding the foot brake continuously causes extreme friction heat and sudden brake loss.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!

question: The minimum safe following distance must be:
options: (1) Greater than.
(2) Less than.
(3) Equal to. the stopping distance.

🎯 Why Choice (1) is Correct: Taiwan Freeway Safety Distance Formula:
• Small Passenger Cars: Speed ÷ 2 in meters ➔ 90 km/h ÷ 2 = 45 meters.
• Large Vehicles (Trucks/Buses): Speed - 20 in meters ➔ 90 km/h - 20 = 70 meters.
Large vehicles have much greater mass and momentum, requiring significantly longer distance to bring to a complete stop.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (2) (Less than.): Incorrect distance calculation that does not provide sufficient emergency reaction and braking buffer.
• Option (3) (Equal to. the stopping distance.): Violates official Highway Bureau safe following distance standards.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Freeway Rule: Small Cars = Speed / 2; Large Trucks = Speed - 20 (double in rain/fog)!

Turning off the engine cuts off the vacuum brake booster and hydraulic power steering, resulting in near-total loss of braking ability and steering control. In addition, shifting to a lower gear utilizes 'Engine Braking', preventing brake pads from overheating and suffering catastrophic brake fade.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!

💡 Pro Study Tip: Engine Oil Check: Level ground + Engine OFF + Wait a few minutes + Level between F and L marks!

question: Which of the following is incorrect regarding how to check engine oil level in a car?

question: Which of the following is the correct way to check the engine oil level?

(2) After turning off the engine, wait a moment for the oil to drain back before checking.
(3) Check while the engine is running.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (2) is Correct: To check engine oil accurately: The car must be parked on LEVEL ground with the engine turned OFF. Wait a few minutes after shutting off the engine so oil circulating in the cylinder head drains back down into the oil pan. Pull the dipstick, wipe it clean, reinsert it fully, and verify the oil level sits between the Upper (F/MAX) and Lower (L/MIN) marks.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (Turn off the engine and check immediately to get the most accurate reading.): Checking immediately or while running gives a falsely low or erratic reading because oil is still actively pumped throughout the engine.
• Option (3) (Check while the engine is running.): Checking on a slope tilts the oil pan and produces a completely inaccurate measurement.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Engine Oil Check: Level ground + Engine OFF + Wait a few minutes + Level between F and L marks!

question: Engine oil, in addition to regular checks:
options: (1) Should be changed periodically.
(2) Does not need to be changed.
(3) Depends on the oil brand.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (1) is Correct: To check engine oil accurately: The car must be parked on LEVEL ground with the engine turned OFF. Wait a few minutes after shutting off the engine so oil circulating in the cylinder head drains back down into the oil pan. Pull the dipstick, wipe it clean, reinsert it fully, and verify the oil level sits between the Upper (F/MAX) and Lower (L/MIN) marks.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (2) (Does not need to be changed.): Checking immediately or while running gives a falsely low or erratic reading because oil is still actively pumped throughout the engine.
• Option (3) (Depends on the oil brand.): Checking on a slope tilts the oil pan and produces a completely inaccurate measurement.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Engine Oil Check: Level ground + Engine OFF + Wait a few minutes + Level between F and L marks!

💡 Pro Study Tip: Downhill Golden Rule: Shift to low gear for Engine Braking; NEVER turn off engine or coast in neutral!
